items.title: Section: The Three Gates of Liberation Close Training

items.zh: 復有三解脫門。一、空解脫門，二、無願解脫門，三、無相解脫門。云何建立三解脫門？謂所知境略有二種。有及非有。有有二種。一者、有為，二者、無為。於有為中，且說三界所繫五蘊；於無為中，且說涅槃。如是二種有為、無為，合說名有。若說於我，或說有情、命者、生者等，是名非有。於有為中見過失故、見過患故，無所祈願；無祈願故，依此建立無願解脫門。於有為中無祈願故，便於涅槃深生祈願，見極寂靜、見甚微妙、見永出離；由於中見永出離故，依此建立無相解脫門。於其非有無所有中，非有祈願、非無祈願；如其非有，還則如是知為非有、見為非有，依此建立空解脫門。
items.en: There are, further, three gates of liberation: the gate of emptiness, the gate of wishlessness, and the gate of signlessness. Seeing fault and defect within conditioned phenomena, one has nothing further to wish for within them — on this basis the gate of wishlessness is established. Having nothing to wish for within conditioned phenomena, one instead wishes deeply for nirvana, seeing it as utterly peaceful, deeply sublime, and a final departure — on this basis, seeing this final departure, the gate of signlessness is established. Regarding the self, which does not exist at all, there is neither wishing nor not-wishing — knowing and seeing it, just as it is, to be non-existent — on this basis the gate of emptiness is established.

items.title: Section: Conduct in Accordance with Training Opens

items.zh: 云何隨順學法？謂有十種違逆學法，對治彼故，應知十種隨順學法。云何十種違逆學法？
items.en: What is conduct in accordance with training? There are ten kinds of conduct that run contrary to training; know that the ten kinds of conduct in accordance with training are simply what counters them.

items.title: Six of the Ten Obstructions to Training

items.zh: 一者、所有母邑少年、盛壯、可愛形色，是正修學善男子等上品障礙。二者、於薩迦耶所攝諸行生起愛著。三者、嬾墮懈怠。四者、薩迦耶見。五者、依於段食貪著美味。六者、於諸世聞種種戲論非一眾多別別品類所思念中，發欲貪愛。
items.en: First: the youthful, vigorous, attractive appearance of women is a severe obstruction for a good son rightly engaged in training. Second: giving rise to attachment towards the formations comprised in the view of a substantial self. Third: laziness and indolence. Fourth: the view of a substantial self. Fifth: craving fine flavour in ordinary food. Sixth: giving rise to desire and craving amid the many varied kinds of worldly idle talk one dwells upon.

items.title: Eleven Faults of Meditative Attention, and the Remaining Obstructions

items.zh: 七者、思惟諸法瑜伽作意所有過患。此復云何？謂十一種。一、於諸諦寶蘊業果中猶預疑惑。二、樂修斷者，身諸麁重。三、有慢緩者，於修止觀過患作意，惛沈睡眠映蔽其心，令心極略。四、太猛精進者，身疲心惱。五、太劣精進者，不得勝進，善品衰退。六、於少利養名譽稱讚隨一樂中，深生欣喜。七、掉舉不靜踊躍躁擾。八、於薩迦耶永滅涅槃而生驚恐。九、於諸言說非量加行，言論太過；雖說法論，而好折伏，起諍方便。十、於先所見、所聞、所受非一眾多別別品類諸境界中，心馳心散。十一、不應思處而強沈思。
items.en: Seventh: the faults belonging to attending, with yogic mental engagement, to the phenomena one contemplates — briefly, eleven kinds: doubt and hesitation regarding the truths, the three jewels, the aggregates, and karma and its fruit; a body weighed down by grossness even while one wishes to cultivate cessation; slackness — the mind covered by torpor and drowsiness, contracted to the barest minimum; excessively forceful effort, leaving body fatigued and mind agitated; excessively feeble effort, gaining no advance and letting wholesome qualities decline; deep delight in even a small gain of support, reputation, or praise; restlessness — unsettled, elated, and agitated; terror at the thought of the substantial self's final cessation in nirvana; excessive argumentative speech, delighting in debate and refutation even while ostensibly discussing the dharma; a mind scattered and racing among the many varied objects previously seen, heard, and experienced; and forcibly dwelling in thought on matters that should not be thought about at all.

items.zh: 應知是名思惟諸法瑜伽作意所有過患。
八者、於諸靜慮、等至樂中深生愛味。九者、樂欲證入無相定者，於諸行中隨順流散。十者、觸身苦受乃至奪命苦受時，貪愛壽命，希望存活；隨此希望，傷歎迷悶。是名十種違逆學法。云何對治如是十種違逆學法隨順學法？
items.en: Eighth: deep attachment to the pleasure found in the absorptions and meditative attainments. Ninth: for one who wishes to enter signless concentration, the mind still scattering outward, drawn along by conditioned formations. Tenth: when touched by bodily suffering — even suffering severe enough to take one's life — clinging to life, hoping to go on living, and, following that hope, falling into grief and confused distress. These are the ten obstructions to training.

items.zh: 謂有十種。一、不淨想，二、無常想，三、無常苦想，四、苦無我想，五、厭逆食想，六、一切世間不可樂想，七、光明想，八、離欲想，九、滅想，十、死想。如是十想，善修、善習、善多修習，能斷十種障礙學法、違逆學法。
items.en: There are ten: the perception of impurity, the perception of impermanence, the perception of impermanence as suffering, the perception of suffering as without self, the perception of aversion towards food, the perception that nothing in the entire world is truly enjoyable, the perception of light, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation, and the perception of death. These ten perceptions, well cultivated, well practised, and thoroughly developed, are able to cut off the ten obstructions to training.

items.zh: 當知此中有四光明。一、法光明，二、義光明，三、奢摩他光明，四、毘鉢舍那光明。依此四種光明增上立光明想。今此義中，意取能斷思惟諸法瑜伽作意障礙法者。當知此中，

blocks.text: The three gates of liberation, then the ten obstructions to training and the ten perceptions that cure them.

**Wishlessness**: "seeing fault within conditioned phenomena, one has nothing further to wish for within them". **Emptiness**: seeing that there is no self in them. Venerable Miào Jìng: "none is found in form, feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness." **Signlessness**: attending to nirvāṇa, free of the signs of the conditioned.

Conduct in accord with training is simply the opposite of ten obstructions: 1. The youthful, attractive appearance of women (the text addresses male monastics). 2. Attachment to the formations grasped as a substantial self. 3. Laziness and indolence. Master Cháng Bǎi: laziness towards good not yet arisen. 4. The view of a substantial self. 5. Craving fine flavours in food. 6. Craving amid worldly idle talk. 7. Eleven faults of meditative attention: doubt about the truths, the Three Jewels, the aggregates, and karma; heaviness of body; slackness and drowsiness; excessive effort ("a string tuned too tight", Master Cháng Bǎi) or too feeble effort; delight in small gains and praise; restlessness; terror at the self's cessation in nirvāṇa; argumentative speech; a scattered mind. 8. Attachment to the pleasure of absorption. 9. The mind scattering towards conditioned formations when trying to enter signless concentration. 10. Clinging to life when touched by severe suffering, and falling into grief.

Impurity, impermanence, impermanence as suffering, suffering as non-self, aversion to food, nothing in the world delightful, light, dispassion, cessation, death. "Well cultivated, they cut off the ten obstructions" in turn. Venerable Miào Jìng: the perception of death is really seeing the quiescence of the aggregates.

quiz.q: On what basis is the gate of wishlessness established, and which contemplations does Venerable Miào Jìng assign to it?
options: seeing fault in the conditioned, wishing for nothing there; impermanence, foulness, and suffering contemplations
quiz.why: "Seeing fault and defect within conditioned phenomena, one has nothing further to wish for within them — on this basis the gate of wishlessness is established." Venerable Miào Jìng: practising contemplation of impermanence, foulness, and suffering all belong to the gate of wishlessness.

quiz.q: What does Venerable Miào Jìng say "liberation" in "three gates of liberation" means?
options: liberation is nirvāṇa; these three are its gates, through which one enters
quiz.why: "The gate of emptiness, the gate of wishlessness, and the gate of signlessness." Venerable Miào Jìng: "liberation" is nirvāṇa; these serve as gates to it, so they are called the three gates of liberation — through them one enters nirvāṇa.

quiz.q: What is the third obstruction, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish 懶惰 from 懈怠?
options: laziness and indolence; laziness is not seeking unarisen good, indolence is slackening in arisen good
quiz.why: "Third: laziness and indolence." Master Cháng Bǎi: laziness concerns good not yet arisen — not bothering to seek it; indolence concerns good already arisen — slackening and not continuing.

quiz.q: Among the faults of meditative attention are too forceful and too feeble effort. What image does Master Cháng Bǎi use?
options: a string tuned too tight cannot achieve the path, nor one too loose
quiz.why: "Excessively forceful effort, leaving body fatigued and mind agitated." Master Cháng Bǎi: a string tuned too tight cannot accomplish the noble path, nor can one tuned too loose.

quiz.q: The ninth obstruction is wishing to enter signless concentration yet scattering among formations. How does Venerable Miào Jìng assess it?
options: this person is somewhat dull in insight; with insight this wouldn't happen
quiz.why: "For one who wishes to enter signless concentration, the mind still scattering outward, drawn along by conditioned formations." Venerable Miào Jìng: this shows the person is somewhat dull in insight; with insight this would not happen.

quiz.q: What are the ten perceptions that counter the obstructions, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the perception of dispassion?
options: impurity, impermanence, impermanence as suffering, suffering as non-self, aversion to food, nothing enjoyable, light, dispassion, cessation, death; absorption isn't final — even craving for form and formless absorptions must be left
quiz.why: "The perception of impurity, of impermanence … of dispassion, of cessation, and of death." Master Cháng Bǎi: absorption is not ultimate either; dispassion means leaving not only desire-realm craving but craving for form and formless absorptions too.

quiz.q: Why does Venerable Miào Jìng say the perception of light is called "light"?
options: affliction is likened to darkness; Dharma, meaning, calm, and insight dispel it — hence "light"
quiz.why: "These ten perceptions, well cultivated, well practised, and thoroughly developed, are able to cut off the ten obstructions to training." Venerable Miào Jìng: afflictions are likened to darkness; the Dharma, its meaning, calm, and insight can dispel that darkness — so they are called light.
